trigger: Suspected security incident affecting Client A information, accounts, or systems, including misuse of the owner's gateway account; suspicious activity seen at a Client A site
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery; suspicious activity at the site at once. Phone first, then in writing
notify: Client A Compliance and Security Coordinator (its FERC primary security contact); Client A OT on-call line
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - always for this incident type

trigger: Any incident that may affect Client B information or the owner's Client B platform account
notify: Client B Chief Dam Safety Engineer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the Client B password or data may have been exposed (the laptop browser held the Client B password)

trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of CEII released under the non-disclosure agreement (upstream project CEII)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the CEII container was open while the malware ran, or any CEII copy was taken. For Client A's CEII, tell Client A under CSCA-A (7) and agree with Client A who tells FERC

obligation: Licensee report of suspicious activity or security incidents to FERC
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, Sec. 3.2 and 4.2
trigger: Suspicious activity or a security incident at the licensee's project
deadline: As soon as practical (usually within one working day)
applies_at_this_tier: No - Client A's duty. The 24-hour notice in row 1 is what lets Client A meet it; the owner supplies facts on request

obligation: Condition affecting safety of project works
trigger: A condition affecting the safety of the project, which includes security incidents (physical and/or cyber)
deadline: Initial report as soon as practicable, preferably within 72 hours; written report as directed
applies_at_this_tier: No - binds applicants and licensees. Client A decides whether its gateway event is reportable; the owner supports with a written timeline

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a high or medium impact BES Cyber System
deadline: (High/medium impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS) Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise an applicable system; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business is not registered, and Client A's project is not a BES generating resource

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR 226.5 (proposed; no dams-specific criterion - via size standard or NERC/OE-417 criterion)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment (proposed)
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; voluntary reporting to CISA is still available

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of a Florida resident (the field assistant's name and Social Security number on the W-9)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the W-9 copy in email or the accounting SaaS was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A vendor maintaining personal information for the business (the accounting SaaS provider) has a breach of security
deadline: No later than 10 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track for the accounting SaaS provider

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency: the only person whose data is held lives in Florida today

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Circumstances that could lead to a claim (for example a client loss from the gateway event)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the policy excludes cyber costs but still asks for notice of circumstances; no cyber policy exists

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
